# cr-2 -- VRRP for the services subnet's floating gateway.
#
# One instance, on eth1 (the services side). eth0 faces management and
# carries no virtual address: the pair is highly available for traffic
# LEAVING the services subnet, which is what a default gateway is for.
# Traffic entering from management names cr-1 or cr-2 directly.
#
# No authentication block. VRRPv2's shared password is not a security
# control -- RFC 5798 dropped it precisely because it authenticates
# nothing against an attacker who can already inject on the segment --
# and this segment is a private bridge with no host address on it.
# Writing one here would look like a control without being one.
#
# preempt is left at its default (on): cr-1 is the designated master by
# priority and takes the address back when it returns, so steady state
# is always the same router, which is the state anything debugging this
# will assume.
global_defs {
    router_id cr-2
}

vrrp_instance services_gw {
    state BACKUP
    interface eth1
    virtual_router_id 150
    priority 100
    advert_int 1
    virtual_ipaddress {
        192.168.150.254/24 dev eth1
    }
}
